neet_phy_u02_t05_1.working: Momentum p = mv has both magnitude and direction and adds by the vector law, so it is a vector. Energy and temperature are scalars, and current is a scalar.

neet_phy_u02_t05_2.working: Currents meeting at a junction add algebraically and do not follow the triangle law of vector addition, so current is a scalar.

neet_phy_u02_t05_3.working: |λA| = |−3| × 5 = 15 units. The negative sign reverses the direction, so the result points opposite to A.

neet_phy_u02_t05_4.working: Equal vectors: same magnitude, same direction (A-III). Negative vector: same magnitude, opposite direction (B-I). Null vector: zero magnitude, arbitrary direction (C-II). Current: has direction but adds algebraically (D-IV).

neet_phy_u02_t05_5.working: A true: a free vector is unchanged by parallel shift. B false: pressure is a scalar. C true: a null vector has zero magnitude and indeterminate direction. D false: work is a dot product, hence a scalar. E true: multiplying by −2 doubles the magnitude and reverses the direction. Correct set is A, C, E.
